policy: UK stochastic assignment contract for the FRS 2024-25 source spine. Date-keyed values use the incumbent parameter loader semantics: choose the latest value with year less than or equal to the build year. Reported-receipt anchors use an unweighted full-population target denominator, target = int(rate * n_units), and accept anchor overshoot. Random streams are intentionally identity-keyed by seed, output variable name, and entity id; this is a signed difference from the incumbent UK pipeline sequential RNG stream. Incumbent provenance: ebf733c.

source.source: Independent Review of Carer's Allowance Overpayments (July 2025), chapter 7, and DWP benefit statistics
source.citation: The share of the carers a reform or a later year newly entitles to Carer's Allowance who claim it. No published rate exists for them: the Independent Review estimates that the April 2025 rise of the earnings limit from 151 to 196 pounds a week brought about 61,000 more people into eligibility, and gives no estimate of how many claim. 0.6 is the central rate of María's ruling of 2026-10-20 (sensitivity 0.45 to 0.75), to be checked against the 61,000 and against DWP's Carer's Allowance caseload by the earnings-limit back-test on the national file (microcosm#1319). Applied by carers_allowance_take_up to a person whose care hours meet the hours condition, who reports no Carer's Allowance and whom the earnings limit holds gainfully employed at the survey year, the year it is keyed at. Scotland's carers take this same rate (María's ruling of 2026-10-23): Carer Support Payment reads the same claim flag, and the contract holds no rate of its own for it.

freeze.decision: María's ruling of 2026-10-20 on the microcosm#1319 plan: a flat 0.6, sensitivity 0.45 to 0.75, with no stage-health gate until a caseload target binds it

source.source: U8 adjudication and upstream issue uk-data#452; lever run receipts in data/ukds/acceptance/757-swap (2026-08-26)
source.citation: Frozen at 0.55 by adjudication for parity with the incumbent UK pipeline. The pre-registered U8 lever (a raise to 0.85 at build year 2024) was run and measured on 2026-08-26 per the #757 uk_target_fit dispositions and REVERTED on the receipts: the raise left every failing UC caseload cell unchanged (dwp.uc.households -44.9% at both rates) while destroying the legacy housing-benefit surface (obr.housing_benefit -0.0% at 0.55, -52.4% at 0.85 - the raise moves claimants off legacy benefits) and polluting the QRF predictor surface through engine-computed household_net_income. The binding constraint on UC caseload is capital-test support (uk-data#452 mechanism 2, microcosm#750), not take-up support. Re-signed 2026-09-16 (#882, microcosm#867): the rate is a share of the benefit units with an adult under State Pension age; units with every adult at or over State Pension age cannot claim Universal Credit (the engine's is_uc_eligible requires a working-age adult) and are no longer drawn, which restores the reported Housing Benefit the draw had zeroed for 407k pension-age units on spine-q; those units have no Universal Credit either way, while the working-age draw moves with the population definition (see below). The 0.55 value is unchanged. Measured on the control and repaired twins at design weights (experiments/882-uc-repairs-receipts.md R5): the old all-units draw realized a 0.582 share among units with a working-age adult, because the reported-UC anchors sit almost entirely there while the count target was taken over every unit; the population draw realizes 0.559 among them and paid UC moves -1.8 percent at design weights. María's ruling of 2026-09-16: keep the rate over the eligible population; the calibrated UC rows absorb the level. Re-signed 2026-10-09 (microcosm#1095, the third ports PR, approved in María's plan of 2026-10-09): the population follows policyengine-uk's is_uc_eligible (2.122.2 when signed; the same in the locked 2.123.0), whose age conditions read the benefit unit's UC claimant or partner (is_uc_claimant) rather than any adult, so a unit whose only member aged 18 to under Pension Credit qualifying age is a dependant is no longer drawn. The 0.55 value is unchanged. Re-signed 2026-10-21 (PolicyEngine/microcosm#1334, María's ruling "lift U8"): for a benefit unit with a Universal Credit award at the calibration year, take-up is no longer this one rate. The uc_take_up spine stage redraws would_claim_uc by DWP family type and monthly award band against DWP Stat-Xplore's calendar-2025 Households on Universal Credit (dwp_uc_award_band_facts.json): reporters claim, and the other entitled units of this population claim at each pooled cell's residual to DWP's count at the spine's design weights over Great Britain. At design weights the one rate put the caseload above DWP's for single people without children, couples and the smallest awards and below it for lone parents, and the national solve met DWP's caseloads by down-weighting low-income families. 0.55 stays the rate frs_take_up and spi_benefit_coherence draw at, which a unit with no award at the calibration year keeps: the rate at which it claims once a reform or a later year entitles it.

freeze.decision: U8 (re-opened and re-frozen by the 2026-08-26 lever run; population re-signed 2026-09-16 to benefit units with an adult under State Pension age, and 2026-10-09 to benefit units with a UC claimant or partner aged 18 to under Pension Credit qualifying age, rate unchanged); lifted 2026-10-21 for entitled units, which uc_take_up draws by award band and family type, the 0.55 rate kept for units with no award

source.source: FRS empirical fit
source.citation: Incumbent offline FRS childcare take-up fit. Conditional rate, nested under the working-parent flag: the share of benefit units not claiming the extended hours that claim the universal hours. A unit that claims the extended hours claims the universal hours with them, so would_claim_universal_childcare = would_claim_extended_childcare OR u < rate and its expected share is r_e + (1 - r_e) * rate. Independent draws let a working-parent unit over the 100k limit hold extended-yes and universal-no, whose child's first 15 hours policyengine-uk then allocates to the universal entitlement only once the limit is removed. The 2024 value below was fitted as an unconditional rate (tool version 4) and is carried unchanged until the childcare fitter refits it on the conditional basis.

source.citation: A calibration adjustment, not a measured routed-expenditure share: an account-active-duration proxy assuming uniform spend through the year and full routing in active months; HMRC warns payment dates need not be care dates. Assigned as the published mean, no invented distribution. Denominator is the whole year; the engine defines the share over the eligible period, and the two coincide while tax_free_childcare_eligible_declaration_periods is 0 or 4. source.source: DfE Apprenticeships statistics, academic year 2024/25, data set 'Geography Region - starts, achievements, participation, population by age, level' (app-geography-population-202425-q4.csv), National rows, apps_level Total, age_summary 19-24
source.derivation: (participation - starts) / population_estimate for England, ages 19 to 24, per academic year, rounded to six decimals: the apprentices already in learning when the year began, per head (2024/25: (252,960 - 97,240) / 4,221,504 = 0.036887)
source.citation: Apprentices in learning at a point in time per head of population aged 19 to 24 in England. DfE publishes no point-in-time count: participation counts everyone in learning at any point in the academic year, so the in-year rate (5,992 per 100,000 in 2024/25) overstates how many are apprentices at once. Participation less the year's starts is the number already in learning on 1 August; in a steady state it is also the year's average number in learning, though autumn starts put the year's low near 1 August. Participation takes age at 31 August and starts take age at the start, so the two differ at the band's edges. DfE publishes no single-year split of 19 to 24, so the rate is taken as uniform across those ages; Medr's single-year Welsh rates fall with age, which points to a lower rate at 21 to 24. England's rate is applied UK-wide until the Scottish (SDS Modern Apprenticeships in training), Welsh (Medr) and Northern Irish (ApprenticeshipsNI) series are added; SDS's point-in-time count is lower per head. frs_person_draws realizes it among employees aged 21 to 24 at the frame's weights.

source.source: DfE 2026 to 2027 early years national funding formulae technical note (3- and 4-year-old additional-hours PTEs, January 2025 censuses) and DfE Education provision: children under 5 years of age, January 2025 (3- and 4-year-olds registered for the working parent entitlement)
source.derivation: 15 + 15 * 341,988.09 additional-hours PTEs / 379,000 registered 3-4-year-olds = 28.535 mean weekly funded hours for a working-parent 3- or 4-year-old (one PTE is 15 hours a week for 38 weeks); mean solves E[clip(N(mean, 4.972), 0, 30)] = 28.535 with the sd and bounds held
source.citation: Replaces the frozen 15.019 / 4.972 incumbent fit (microcosm#834), which #834 held pending evidence on hours actually used. The DfE additional-hours PTEs are that evidence: observed January 2025 census volumes, not a forecast. The variable caps a family's total weekly extended hours, so its mean is the total (universal plus additional) for a 3- or 4-year-old. Only the 3-4 cohort anchors the mean; DfE's under-2 and 2-year-old PTEs are partly forecast. The sd is not identified by any source and keeps the incumbent value. Re-mapping the 2024-25 national release's own draws through this distribution gives 2026-27 free-entitlement spending of 9.30bn against DfE's illustrative 9.9bn (5.81bn before); see microcosm#1126.
